fake.banner: Dry run: demo mode, no model (not the published video)

notes: The README video (decision 0027): a real model, so the rows are matched flexibly. Each row is shown at most once, on the first matching event; an unexpected tool call or a validator error gets a generic row; rows that never match are listed in out/groq/take.json.
{name}: VIDEO_DESIGN_NAME (default 'Amber Lantern'; the app adds the family suffix 'Faceted'), a name not in the SAP seed, so the take shows no taken-name warning.

Payloads come only from the take's capture: SSE events, the JSON of POST /api/actions, .../confirm and /api/preview (the panel's check), the run's trace, or introspect.py (read only). Callouts are [file, symbol], resolved by lines.mjs at take time.
The FreeCAD rows (6.2-6.4) are in cues-freecad.json: the clip is recorded on the desktop and composed in where it ran.

sentences.question: Why are 32 facets per row too many for a 10 mm bead?
sentences.design: A 10 mm faceted amber bead for the Amber Hollow collection
sentences.reserve: Reserve a SKU for it as {name} Faceted

rows.subtitle: Bead Studio: a designer describes a bead; a real model guides, the code decides.
First, a question about a rule of the Product Design Manual.
The model picks a tool: a search of the manual, with its own keywords.
SQLite full-text search ranks the sections (BM25, headings weigh more); the rule comes back as text.
The model answers from the passage and cites the rule. The numbers come from the tools.
Now a new bead, in one sentence.
The model proposes numbers for the parameter panel.
The validators decide. Amber marks what the assistant proposed; the designer can change any value.
CadQuery builds the solid; the 3D view, the volume and the mass come from it.
The designer types 32 facets per row by hand.
The same validators answer: rule GB-05, and the nearest valid values. The model can explain a rule; it cannot overrule it.
One click takes the nearest valid value.
The designer asks for a SKU.
Without a model, the panel's Reserve SKU form opens the same card (dry run only).
The model can only open a card. Nothing reaches SAP until the designer clicks Confirm.
The click calls the confirm endpoint. Only SapClient talks to SAP (OData v2, CSRF token).
SAP issues the next SKU and material number. The reservation is in the audit log.
Generate: a second card, from the numbers in the panel.
The click checks the rules again, then CadQuery writes STEP, STL and GLB inside the designs folder only.
And a drawing: OpenCascade hidden-line views on a sheet with the H&L title block.
SKU, revision, SAP material, scale and mass in the title block, from the same numbers.
A third click queues a catalog render. Blender runs headless, one job at a time, while…
The catalog render, from Blender headless, followed live (server-sent events).
The AI guides. The code decides. The designer clicks.
